title: The postcards, not bought
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The drugstore's postcard slot, restocked for Christmas. Wood looks at it. Seven in the drawer at home; one in the box. He doesn't buy. The clerk says nothing this year. The clerk reads. He knows what seven means.

panels.composition: The drugstore's card rack. The postcard slot: the bay, faded blue, full. WOOD looking at it. BARNABY. The CLERK at the register.

image.prompt: a young man in a chore coat looking at a drugstore rack slot full of identical faded postcards while a clerk watches from the register, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The postcards. Full slot. Wood's hand not reaching.

image.prompt: close on a rack slot of identical postcards with a young man's hand hovering but not reaching, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The clerk. Saying nothing. Knowing seven.

image.prompt: a drugstore clerk at a register saying nothing, knowing, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood out the door without a card. Seven in the drawer. One in the box. The clerk reads; he knows the arithmetic. The strip does it again anyway: seven, one, two sent. Ten.

image.prompt: a young man in a chore coat leaving a drugstore empty-handed with a small dog, black and white, no words

notes: Seven, one, two. The clerk knows the arithmetic.
